b_records.quote: Theorem 2: Let X1 ~ APTQLD(alpha1,beta1,theta1) and X2 ~ APTQLD(alpha2,beta2,theta2). If alpha1 < alpha2, beta1 = beta2 = beta and theta1 = theta2 = theta, then X1 <=lr X2. [Proof:] It is certain that for alpha1 < alpha2, beta1 = beta2 = beta and theta1 = theta2 = theta, d log(f1(x)/f2(x))/dx < 0. Under these conditions, X1 is stochastically smaller than X2 in the likelihood ratio order.
b_records.family: APTQLD(alpha,beta,theta) - alpha power transformation of quasi Lindley distribution
b_records.compared: two APTQLD variables differing only in the alpha power parameter

hypotheses.text: alpha1 < alpha2, beta1 = beta2 = beta, theta1 = theta2 = theta

b_records.quantifiers: x > 0; parameters alpha > 1 (log alpha appears), beta > -1, theta > 0
b_records.ambiguity: Proof shows d/dx log(f1/f2) < 0 under the stated equal-parameter conditions; algebraic details are OCR-corrupted in the extracted text.

records.quote: X1 is smaller than X2 in: a) stochastic order (X1 <=st X2) if R1(x,alpha1,beta1,theta1) <= R2(x,alpha2,beta2,theta2); b) hazard rate order (X1 <=hr X2) if h1(x)/h2(x) is decreasing in x; c) mean residual life order (X1 <=mrl X2) if E(X1-t|X1<t) <= E(X2-t|X2<t); d) likelihood ratio order (X1 <=lr X2) if f1(x)/f2(x) is a decreasing function of x. Notably, if X1 <=lr X2, then X1 <=hr X2, X1 <=mrl X2 and X1 <=st X2.
records.family: alpha power transformed quasi Lindley distribution APTQLD(alpha, beta, theta)

conclusion.direction: lr order implies hr, mrl and st orders (X1 <=lr X2 => X1 <=hr X2, X1 <=mrl X2, X1 <=st X2)

records.ambiguity: Definitions copied verbatim; the mrl definition is printed with E(X-t|X<t) which is the reversed (mean inactivity) conditioning, a likely typo for the standard mrl conditioning X > t.
